subject: Chemistry
title: The Deepwater Horizon Spill
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Deepwater Horizon Spill.

hook.text: In 2010, the Deepwater Horizon oil rig exploded, killing 11 workers and releasing 780 million liters of oil into the Gulf.

buildup.text: A blowout preventer failed, and high-pressure oil and gas surged up the drill pipe from 1,500 meters below the seafloor.

discovery.text: BP used 7 million liters of chemical dispersant to break up the oil. The dispersant itself proved toxic to marine life.

twist.text: The well leaked for 87 days before being capped. It was the largest accidental marine oil spill in history.

climax.text: BP paid $65 billion in cleanup costs and fines. The spill devastated Gulf fishing and tourism for years.

punchline.text: A failed valve, 87 days of gushing oil. The cure was almost as toxic as the spill.

quiz.question: What problem arose from using chemical dispersants on the Deepwater Horizon spill?
options: The dispersant itself proved toxic to marine life
The dispersant caused the oil to solidify and sink
Dispersants attracted more oil from neighboring wells

details.summary: The 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster killed 11 workers and released nearly five million barrels of crude oil into the Gulf of Mexico over 87 days. A failed blowout preventer and cement seal allowed high-pressure oil and gas to surge up the wellbore and ignite on the drilling platform.
details.whyItMatters: Deepwater Horizon was the largest marine oil spill in history and exposed the chemical complexity of oil dispersants, seafloor ecology, and deep-water drilling risks.
takeaways: Nearly five million barrels of oil leaked over 87 days
The blowout preventer failed to seal the well as designed
Corexit dispersants broke oil into droplets with debated long-term effects

faq.question: What role did chemistry play in the cleanup of the Deepwater Horizon spill?
faq.answer: Millions of liters of Corexit dispersant were sprayed to break oil into tiny droplets that bacteria could degrade faster. This was the largest use of dispersants in history. The chemistry reduced surface oil but raised concerns about subsurface toxicity and long-term ecosystem effects.

faq.question: Why did the blowout preventer fail to stop the leak?
faq.answer: Investigations found that the blowout preventer's shear rams were not powerful enough to cut through the drill pipe, which had buckled under pressure. Dead batteries, design limitations, and inadequate testing all contributed to the critical safety device's failure during the emergency.
